Upgrading from older versions

Source: vignettes/migrate.Rmd
migrate.Rmd

Read this page if you have code written for readgpt, the package’s name up to version 0.6.0, or for its first version (v1). Each table lists an old name, the name that replaced it and what to change in your code. None of the old names has an alias: calling an old function stops with “could not find function”. NEWS.md lists every change release by release.

The files listed under “What still loads”, at the end of this page, still load. A response cache written by readgpt 0.5.1 or earlier is not read.

From readgpt 0.6.0: core functions now start with hr_

The 27 core functions that began with gr_ now begin with hr_, like the rest of the core layer. Document-layer functions such as gr_read(), gr_ingest() and gr_extract() keep gr_, so replace only the names in this table. A blanket search and replace of gr_ breaks them.

Old New What to change
gr_api_key() hr_api_key() Rename the call.
gr_backend_client() hr_backend_client() Rename the call.
gr_budget() hr_budget() Rename the call.
gr_cache() hr_cache() Rename the call.
gr_cache_clear() hr_cache_clear() Rename the call.
gr_cache_client() hr_cache_client() Rename the call.
gr_cache_stats() hr_cache_stats() Rename the call.
gr_call() hr_call() Rename the call.
gr_client() hr_client() Rename the call.
gr_count_tokens() hr_count_tokens() Rename the call.
gr_ellmer_client() hr_ellmer_client() Rename the call.
gr_embed() hr_embed() Rename the call.
gr_estimate_cost() hr_estimate_cost() Rename the call.
gr_mock_client() hr_mock_client() Rename the call.
gr_model_info() hr_model_info() Rename the call.
gr_model_limits() hr_model_limits() Rename the call.
gr_models() hr_models() Rename the call.
gr_options() hr_options() Rename the call.
gr_register_model() hr_register_model() Rename the call.
gr_replay_client() hr_replay_client() Rename the call.
gr_set_tokenizer() hr_set_tokenizer() Rename the call.
gr_tokenizer() hr_tokenizer() Rename the call.
gr_trace() hr_trace() Rename the call.
gr_trace_cost() hr_trace_cost() Rename the call.
gr_trace_save() hr_trace_save() Rename the call.
gr_trace_summary() hr_trace_summary() Rename the call.
gr_truncate_tokens() hr_truncate_tokens() Rename the call.

The objects these functions return keep their gr_ classes. Code that tests inherits(x, "gr_client") or handles a gr_call_cap condition works as before.

Before and after

Most scripts written for 0.6.0 make a client, call it and read the trace. In 0.6.0 that read:

library(readgpt)
cl <- gr_mock_client(function(messages, params) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
tr <- gr_trace()
res <- gr_call(cl, "What was revenue?", trace = tr)
gr_trace_summary(tr)$calls

Now it reads as below. The package name and the four core calls change; the arguments, the reply and the class stay the same:

library(harnessr)
old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE)
cl <- hr_mock_client(function(messages, params) "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars.")
tr <- hr_trace()
res <- hr_call(cl, "What was revenue?", trace = tr)
res$text
#> [1] "Revenue was 45.2 million dollars."
hr_trace_summary(tr)$calls
#> [1] 1
inherits(cl, "gr_mock_client")
#> [1] TRUE

From readgpt 0.6.0: the package, options and other removed names

harnessr was called readgpt up to version 0.6.0, and so was its GitHub repository. The rename itself changes no request or key. This release does move the response cache to the key harnessr-cache-v3 and replay to harnessr-replay-v2; “What still loads” says how old entries are found.

Old New What to change
readgpt harnessr Load it with library(harnessr) and install it with remotes::install_github("elkronos/harnessr"). GitHub sends the old repository address to the new one.
readgpt_example() gr_example() Rename the call. It returns the same path to the bundled example document.
options(readgpt.api_key =) options(harnessr.api_key =) Rename the option. harnessr ignores the old one, so a key set only there is not found.
options(readgpt.allow_local_urls =) options(harnessr.allow_local_urls =) Rename the option. harnessr ignores the old one.
gr_calibrate()’s $kappa_legacy gr_calibrate()’s $kappa Read $kappa. $decisions holds the 3x2 counts the old figure came from.
the gr_deprecated warning class none Drop handlers for it. Nothing warns about an old name now.

From v1

v1, the package’s first version, had six entry points that 0.2.0 replaced and later versions removed. Each has a replacement:

Old New What to change
answer_question() answer_document() answer_question(f, q, mode = "Chunked") becomes answer_document(f, q, "thorough"). To run several recipes on one document, use gr_compare().
parse_text() gr_ingest(), then gr_segment() parse_text(f, chunk_method = "semantic") becomes gr_segment(gr_ingest(f), "semantic", client = cl). Semantic chunking embeds, so it needs a client; without one it warns and cuts paragraphs.
gpt_read_chunked() gr_read() Segment first, then call gr_read(chunks, q, cl, "map_reduce").
gpt_read_retrieval() gr_read() Segment first, then call gr_read(chunks, q, cl, "skim").
gpt_read_hierarchical() gr_read() Segment first, then call gr_read(chunks, q, cl, "hierarchical").
gpt_read_multipass() gr_read() Segment first, then call gr_read(chunks, q, cl, "ensemble").

Three behaviour changes from v1 are deliberate and will alter your results:

  1. mode no longer defaults to all five modes. answer_question(f, q) in v1 ran every mode: 41 API calls on an 8-paragraph document, where one was expected.
  2. Modes no longer contaminate each other. In v1, mode = c("Chunked", "Semantic") changed Chunked’s chunking, its cost, and its answer relative to mode = "Chunked" alone.
  3. Digits are no longer stripped by default. v1’s remove_numbers = TRUE default was unreachable from answer_question(), so every figure, date and percentage was deleted before the model saw the document.

For v1’s refine = TRUE, ask for citations with cite = TRUE in gr_read_spec(). Its verification pass has no replacement because it could not run: it called a search_text() function that the repository never defined.

The v1 source is kept under legacy/ in the repository for reference and A/B comparison. The package does not load it. To reproduce its ingestion and chunking under the current code, use the legacy recipe. It strips digits, as v1 did, and cuts 3000-token paragraph chunks with no overlap:

old <- hr_options(verbose = FALSE)
legacy <- gr_recipes("legacy")
gr_ingest("Revenue was 45.2 million dollars in fiscal 2024.", legacy$ingest)$text
#> [1] "Revenue was . million dollars in fiscal ."
unlist(legacy$segment[c("method", "max_tokens", "overlap_tokens")])
#>         method     max_tokens overlap_tokens 
#>    "paragraph"         "3000"            "0"

The regression suite in tests/testthat/ reproduces each of these defects against the current code.

What still loads

harnessr writes new cache entries under the key harnessr-cache-v3 and records replay steps under harnessr-replay-v2. When a call finds nothing under the new key, harnessr looks it up under the old one, and a reply found that way raises an hr_legacy_key warning. Each item below names the test in tests/testthat/ that loads such a file.

  • Response caches. A cache written by readgpt 0.6.0, or by an earlier build of harnessr, answers every call it holds through the old key readgpt-cache-v2, and nothing is sent. The warning comes once per cache in a session. A call with a draw index does not read the old keys. readgpt 0.5.1 and earlier wrote the key readgpt-cache-v1, which harnessr does not read, so the calls in such a cache are sent again. Tests: “an old cache answers every call through the old key, each hit warning” and “an old cache is not read for a draw”, in test-compat-legacy-keys.R.
  • readgpt’s cache directory. When your cache directory is tools::R_user_dir("harnessr", "cache"), entries readgpt kept in tools::R_user_dir("readgpt", "cache") answer too, after it. harnessr never writes to or clears the old directory. Test: “entries readgpt kept in its documented cache directory still answer”, in test-compat-legacy-keys.R.
  • Traces and replay recordings (cassettes). A trace saved by gr_trace_save() in 0.6.0 replays with hr_replay_client(), strict mode included. Test: “an old recording replays strictly through the old key, each hit warning”, in test-compat-legacy-keys.R. A trace’s meta still records the version under readgpt, so traces from before and after the rename read the same way. Test: “a trace records the configuration that produced it, not just the recipe’s name”, in test-hardening.R.
  • Signal calibrations. Calibrations keep their own contract version, 0.1, so a record saved under 0.1 stays valid. Test: “a calibration key keeps contract version 0.1, so a saved record stays valid”, in test-contract-02.R.
  • Stores. A gr_read_many() store written by an older version resumes. Tests: “a store written by an older version still resumes”, in test-corpus.R, and “a store entry written by 0.5.0 is read again once, then restored”, in test-review3-corpus.R.
  • Class names. Objects keep their gr_ classes, so an object saved before the rename still dispatches. Tests: “the renamed constructors still make gr_ classes” and “a gr_result saved before the rename prints with its method”, in test-core-names.R.
